item.title: CISA adds Ivanti Connect Secure SAML single sign on bypass CVE-2026-128501 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog directives under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, issuing an emergency remediation order for an actively weaponized remote access gateway flaw. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit single sign-on logic flaws within SAML assertion parsing subroutines to obtain administrative execution across edge gateways.
The emergency security directive addresses Ivanti Connect Secure ICS and Policy Secure IPS vulnerability CVE-2026-128501 carrying a CVSS score of 9.9. Unauthenticated remote adversaries send crafted SAML authentication requests to exposed web portals, bypassing authentication handlers and triggering command injection routines with root privileges. Threat telemetry confirms nation-state threat actors actively weaponize the flaw to plant persistent web shells and extract SSL VPN session tokens. CISA established a mandatory December 14 compliance deadline for Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to deploy emergency patches.
Subverting central remote access controllers undermines network perimeter boundaries and enterprise identity governance. Because Ivanti Connect Secure manages corporate VPN connections and zero-trust remote access, an unauthenticated root compromise allows threat actors to intercept internal transit traffic, harvest user credentials, and move laterally across internal subnets.
- Apply official Ivanti security release updates immediately across all deployed Connect Secure and Policy Secure gateway appliances. - Run the official Integrity Checker Tool ICT to inspect system file trees for unauthorized web shell scripts or backdoor modifications. - Restrict public internet exposure of administrative web management portals, routing management interfaces behind out-of-band VLANs. - Invalidate active remote access user session tokens and execute mandatory credential rotations across corporate VPN user accounts.
Secure access gateway defense requires immediate software patch application and rigorous file integrity monitoring to ensure perimeter remote connections remain protected against unauthenticated command execution exploits. #CodeDefence #Ivanti #ConnectSecure #PolicySecure #ZeroDay #RCE #SAML #CommandInjection #CISA #KEV #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Active zero day exploitation targets GitLab GraphQL API integer overflow vulnerability CVE-2026-127110
item.description:
DevSecOps platform maintainers have published security advisories warning of active wild exploitation targeting self-hosted code repositories. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit integer overflow vulnerabilities in API query subroutines to bypass access controls and trigger remote code execution.
The security advisory addresses GitLab Community Edition CE and Enterprise Edition EE vulnerability CVE-2026-127110 carrying a CVSS score of 9.9. Remote unauthenticated threat actors transmit malformed GraphQL API requests containing nested integer arrays to trigger heap buffer overflows in backend parser subroutines. Exploitation allows adversaries to execute arbitrary commands under the git user context, extract proprietary repository source code, and compromise CI CD pipeline environment variables. GitLab issued emergency security release versions 17.5.2, 17.4.4, and 17.3.7 to remediate exposed deployments.
Subverting central DevOps code repositories introduces severe supply-chain risks across software development pipelines. Because GitLab hosts enterprise source code repositories and manages automated CI CD deployment runners, an unauthenticated RCE permits threat actors to inject malicious backdoors into production builds and harvest deployment API secrets.
- Upgrade self-hosted GitLab CE EE instances immediately to emergency patch releases 17.5.2, 17.4.4, or 17.3.7. - Restrict public network access to GraphQL API endpoints, placing self-hosted GitLab servers behind zero-trust access proxies. - Rotate all CI CD pipeline variables, production deployment keys, and personal access tokens stored within affected GitLab projects. - Inspect GitLab runner execution logs and web server access records for anomalous GraphQL POST requests originating from untrusted IP ranges.
DevOps platform security requires rapid patch deployment and strict API exposure management to ensure central source code repositories and CI CD pipelines remain protected against unauthenticated remote code execution. #CodeDefence #GitLab #GraphQL #IntegerOverflow #ZeroDay #RCE #SupplyChain #DevSecOps #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA

item.title: Critical Brotli Node2Shell library vulnerability CVE-2026-111497 exploited in wild automated server scanning campaigns
item.description:
Threat intelligence feeds published today report massive automated scanning campaigns targeting exposed web runtimes and reverse proxies. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit buffer overflow flaws in open-source data compression libraries to execute remote code across web server clusters.
The threat warning details accelerated wild exploitation targeting Brotli compression library vulnerability CVE-2026-111497, codenamed Node2Shell, carrying a CVSS score of 9.8. Unauthenticated remote adversaries send crafted compressed stream headers to trigger out-of-bounds heap memory corruption within Node.js runtimes, web application servers, and reverse proxy gateways. Threat research confirms automated botnets are scanning public IPv4 subnets to deploy cryptocurrency miners and persistent web shell backdoors. CISA previously mandated federal agency compliance under BOD 22-01.
Subverting core data compression libraries poses widespread systemic risks across public cloud hosting environments and web application runtimes. Because Brotli handles web content compression across web servers, API gateways, and microservices, an unauthenticated heap corruption RCE allows remote threat actors to compromise host web servers and pivot laterally into internal microservice networks.
- Update Brotli library dependencies immediately across Node.js web application runtimes, container base images, and reverse proxy web servers. - Configure Web Application Firewalls WAF to inspect HTTP compression headers and drop malformed Brotli stream payloads at the edge. - Inspect application runtime memory logs for unverified segmentation faults or process crashes originating from decompression subroutines. - Enforce strict egress network filtering on application server hosts to block unauthorized outbound connections to command and control servers.
Application runtime defense demands immediate software dependency updates and rigid edge payload inspection to ensure enterprise web services remain insulated from unauthenticated memory corruption exploits. #CodeDefence #Brotli #Node2Shell #Nodejs #RCE #HeapCorruption #WebSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA #CloudSecurity
